chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from ‘Abdullāh ibn Idrīs, from Muhammad ibn Sinān, from Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the knowledge of the Imam concerning what is in the regions of the earth while he is in his house with his curtain let down over him.

He said: O Mufaḍḍal, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, placed within the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله five spirits: the spirit of life, by which he moved and progressed; the spirit of strength, by which he rose and strove; the spirit of desire, by which he ate, drank, and approached women through what is halal; the spirit of faith, by which he believed and acted justly; and the Holy Spirit, by which he bore prophethood.

Then when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is taken, the Holy Spirit passes on and comes to the Imam. The Holy Spirit neither sleeps, nor becomes heedless, nor engages in diversion, nor exults; while the four spirits sleep, become heedless, exult, and engage in diversion. And it was by the Holy Spirit that he would see.

key_terms.أَقْطَارِ الْأَرْضِ: the regions and far reaches of the earth
key_terms.النُّبُوَّةَ: prophethood, borne through the Holy Spirit
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَرْوَاحٍ: five spirits placed within the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.رُوحَ الْإِيمَانِ: the spirit by which faith and justice are realized
key_terms.رُوحَ الْحَيَاةِ: the spirit by which bodily life and movement occur
key_terms.رُوحَ الْقُدُسِ: the Holy Spirit by which prophethood is borne and which passes to the Imam
key_terms.رُوحَ الْقُوَّةِ: the spirit by which rising and striving are enabled
key_terms.عِلْمِ الْإِمَامِ: the Imam’s knowledge concerning realities beyond ordinary sensory access

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Imam’s knowledge of what is across the earth while he remains in his house?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, granted the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله five spirits, each associated with a distinct function, including the Holy Spirit through which he bore prophethood. It further states that after the Prophet’s passing, the Holy Spirit passes to the Imam, indicating a divinely granted mode of awareness and authority connected to the office of Imamate.
